intended_object: For a height sequence h : ℕ → ℝ ∪ {∞}, the set of indices n such that both h n and h (n+1) are finite, i.e. the genuine unit edges [n, n+1] of the finite domain on which a real slope is defined (from the docstring and its use in IsConvexSeq).
explanation: The body {n | h n ≠ ⊤ ∧ h (n + 1) ≠ ⊤} is exactly the set the docstring describes. It is used to restrict the monotonicity of the real increments unitSlope in IsConvexSeq, so that the junk value untop₀ ⊤ = 0 is never treated as a slope. Degenerate cases behave as intended. If all heights are ⊤ or only one height is finite, the set is empty. If the finite domain is a half-line, the set is the matching half-line. The body does not depend on ℝ (it would work for WithTop α), but the whole module is set up for real heights in WithTop ℝ, as its later use of real slopes and sums requires. For a helper set this is the natural choice, not a loss of generality. Mathlib has no matching definition.
